newsitem.title: INDIA: India gem, jewellery exports slow in Apr'96-Jan'97.
newsitem.headline: India gem, jewellery exports slow in Apr'96-Jan'97.

text.p: India's year-on-year gem and jewellery export growth slowed during April 1996-January 1997 due to a decline in demand and a fall in export prices, the government said on Monday.

Gem and jewellery exports totalled a provisional $4.1 billion in the ten months to January, down from $4.3 billion during April 1995-January 1996, Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah told the upper house of parliament in a written statement.
He said gem and jewellery exports had risen substantially in the last three years.

"However, this year in the period April-Jan 1997 some deceleration in export growth has been noticed due to overall decline in demand for both diamonds and studded jewellery and also due to fall in FOB (freight-over-board) prices of cut and polished diamonds," Ramaiah said.
He said diamond exports during the period had fallen to a provisional $3.4 billion, from $3.7 billion in the year-earlier period.
Gold jewellery exports rose to $540.08 million in April 1996-December 1997, from $466.36 million in the year-earlier period.
Ramaiah said the government had taken a number of steps to boost exports in this sector.
These included lowering interest rates on post-shipment credit and allowing authorised dealers to receive import documents upto $25,000 by value or its equivalent directly from the overseas seller.
